chunks: He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated to me. He said: al-Hasan ibn Aleel al-Anzi narrated to us. He said: Abdul Karim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Manqar narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn al-Munzir. He said: Sharjeel narrated to us, from Umm al-Fadhl ibn al-Abbas.

She said: When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his progeny, fell seriously ill in his final illness, he woke up briefly while we were crying around him. He said: 'What makes you cry?' We said: 'O Messenger of God, we cry not for one reason; we cry because you will leave us, because the heavenly news will cease to come to us, and we cry for the Ummah after you.' Then he said, peace be upon him and his progeny: 'Be it clear to you that you will be the suppressed and the weakened after me.'

key_terms.المستضعفون: The weakened - those denied rightful authority
key_terms.المقهورون: The suppressed - prophetic term for Ahl al-Bayt's post-prophetic fate
key_terms.خبر السماء: News from heaven - divine revelation through the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the fate of Ahlul Bayt after his death?
ai.summary: Umm al-Fadhl narrates that when the Prophet (SAWA) fell seriously ill in his final days, he briefly regained consciousness while his household wept around him. When he asked why they cried, they mentioned three reasons: his impending departure, the cessation of divine revelation, and concern for the Ummah. The Prophet confirmed their fears, foretelling that his Ahl al-Bayt would be suppressed and weakened after him.
